Plot Directional (Signed) Feature Importance for a Mossy Forest Object

Source: R/shapff_plot.R
plot_signed_importance.Rd

Bar chart of signed importance = direction \(\times\) mean|SHAP|. Magnitude is mean|SHAP| and the sign is the global effect direction taken from the Spearman correlation between each feature's value and its SHAP value (mean(signed SHAP) \(\approx 0\) because contributions cancel, so it is unusable for direction). Bars to the right increase the average predicted outcome, and bars to the left decrease it. These are associations in the fitted model, not causal effects of changing a feature. Features whose direction is ambiguous (non monotone: \(|\rho| < 0.1\)) are greyed. For binary classification, "the outcome" means the probability of levels(y)[1], the first level of the factor passed as y to mf. Relevel y first if you want a different reference class.

Usage

plot_signed_importance(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mossy_forest'
plot_signed_importance(
  object,
  top_n = 20L,
  labels = NULL,
  pos_color = "#4393c3",
  neg_color = "#d6604d",
  amb_color = "#bbbbbb",
  pos_label = "increase",
  neg_label = "decrease",
  amb_label = "ambiguous",
  main = "Directional feature importance",
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A mossy_forest object.

...

Ignored.

top_n

Show only the top_n features with the largest \(|\)signed importance\(|\). Default 20L; use NULL or Inf to plot every stable feature.

labels

Optional named character vector mapping feature names (as in final_SHAP$feature_name) to readable labels for the axis, e.g. a gene symbol or indicator name lookup. Names not found are left unchanged. Default NULL (show the raw feature names).

pos_color

Bar color for positive direction. Default "#4393c3".

neg_color

Bar color for negative direction. Default "#d6604d".

amb_color

Bar color for ambiguous features. Default "#bbbbbb".

pos_label

Legend text for the positive direction group. Default "increase".

neg_label

Legend text for the negative direction group. Default "decrease".

amb_label

Legend text for the ambiguous group. Default "ambiguous".

main

Plot title. Default "Directional feature importance".

Value

A ggplot2 object (invisibly).

Methods (by class)

  • plot_signed_importance(mossy_forest): Signed importance plot for a mossy_forest object.

Examples

# A small simulated regression problem with two modules of features
set.seed(1)
n <- 60
z <- rnorm(n)
X <- data.frame(a1 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), a2 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3),
                a3 = z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), b1 = rnorm(n), b2 = rnorm(n),
                b3 = rnorm(n))
y <- z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
membership <- c(a1 = "A", a2 = "A", a3 = "A", b1 = "B", b2 = "B", b3 = "B")

# The pure R backend needs no Python installation
fit <- mf(X, y, module_membership = membership,
          screen_params = screen_control(min_ntree = 50),
          select_params = select_control(n_reps = 10, min_ntree = 50),
          final_ntree = 50, backend = "R", r_shap = "treeshap", verbose = 0, seed = 1)
plot_signed_importance(fit)
